source_sequence.focus: Employer encounter — skills, recruitment and belonging

source_adaptation: I15 calls for preparation, clear outcomes, two-way employer/employee interaction and structured reflection. It specifies no phase minutes. The 5/5/12/10/8 classroom example is an adaptation. Allow a longer or separate real encounter if needed; prepare before and reflect after it. Profile simulation and recording alone are learning sources, not proof of a real employer encounter. The user adds a seven-week portfolio close to J15.
success: Explain one valued skill with evidence.
Explain recruitment steps and selection evidence.
Explain one workplace support and how it helps someone succeed.
prepare: Books, pens, profile A/B, question menu, vocabulary, evidence record and the seven weeks of work already held. Have the Autumn 1 personal career profile ready if available. Staff may use a visitor or approved local recording with captions/transcript. No visitor or recording is supplied. Without either, use the complete printed role-play.
activity: Prepare evidence-based questions and rehearse. Use visitor, recording or full employer-profile simulation. Explain skills, recruitment and support, reflect against earlier personal profile, retain feedback/revision and review all seven portfolio outputs.

evidence.description: Employer-encounter reflection linked to personal profile: source-based explanation of a valued skill, recruitment process/selection evidence, and one support with its effect. Link to an actual earlier personal career profile; missing history stays a gap. Seven-week portfolio index records actual references, held/partial/missing status, quality checks and next actions. Keep source/mode, real contact status, access, answer prompts and revision separately.
Seven-week portfolio index with actual work references, evidence status, quality checks, gaps and one dated next action.

evidence_detail: Employer-encounter reflection linked to personal profile: source-based explanation of a valued skill, recruitment process/selection evidence, and one support with its effect. Link to an actual earlier personal career profile; missing history stays a gap. Seven-week portfolio index records actual references, held/partial/missing status, quality checks and next actions. Keep source/mode, real contact status, access, answer prompts and revision separately.
assessment: N15 S: assess the three exact outcome parts using actual source evidence. Record secure, partial or not yet for valued skill, recruitment and workplace support separately. M15 checks a recruitment insight and valued skill with encounter evidence; the exact outcome also requires workplace support. The new reflection links to the earlier personal career profile.
boundaries: Generic employer types only. Profiles are invented, not offers, universal recruitment rules or support guarantees. No actual learner history or attendance is prefilled. No public personal disclosure or real practical work. Use controlled references instead of adding named employers to the distributed pack.
feedback: VF verbal feedback · WS worked with support · I independent · NS next step in green · // self-edit · ? read this back · E actual banked evidence · R only after Voice, Audience, NS and a response in the learner’s in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.
response_modes: Book first. Optional Type instead carries the same demand. Record usual access separately from answer prompts. Set one NS, allow a learner revision and preserve first thinking. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

routes.Independent: Select source evidence for a valued skill, explain the recruitment sequence and selection evidence, and show how one support helps. Compare with the earlier personal profile and keep a next question. Locate all seven portfolio outputs and identify any gap.
routes.Supported: Read one profile section or talk section at a time. Use the question menu, separate model, word bank and three explanation headings. Rehearse privately. Fade answer frames where secure. Keep the learner’s own explanation and portfolio judgements.
routes.Floor: Use A and short choices. Read or scribe the learner’s own response. Then ask them to explain the chosen skill with a clue, place recruitment steps in order, and say how a support helps. Choices alone are partial. Adult help finding work can support portfolio access without deciding the evidence judgement.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Use explicit instruction, a worked model, guided practice and a visible sequence. Chunk the profile into role, skill, recruitment and support. Keep a checklist and use retrieval from actual earlier work. Allow processing time.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Pre-teach employer, recruitment, evidence and belonging. Use private rehearsal, written questions, a scribe or relay of the learner’s own words. Check access to replies. No cold calling. Accept speech, writing, pointing with explanation, or normal communication aids.
adaptations.SEMH: Explain who will speak and how the session will run. No forced public disclosure of grades, diagnosis, family employment or income. Allow a private view, a regulation break and a clear return point. Missing portfolio work is an action to plan, not a public judgement.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Use clear print, captions/transcript, accessible seating and normal aids. Check hearing, sightlines and comfort. The lesson uses source reading only; no bakery equipment, lifting, machinery or practical workplace task is required.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Use the vocabulary and short frames, pause the source and check key meanings. Separate language access from careers understanding. Normal reading/scribing aids continue while answer scaffolds fade.

hinge: A learner says “I applied, so I have the job.” A agree, or B staff still select and check evidence before an offer decision? B. If any learner is unsure, sequence the profile steps with them before independent explanation. If secure, ask why the task provides relevant evidence.
parallel_hinge: “A checklist means nobody can make a mistake.” A agree, or B it can help someone spot a missed check but does not guarantee success? B. If insecure, model support plus likely effect and a limit, then revisit a different example.
frames: Floor: “They value ... . The card says ... .” Medium: “First ... then ... . Staff use ... to choose.” High: “This support may help because ... . My earlier profile said ... . I now think ... because ... .”
misconceptions: A skill label alone is not an evidence-based explanation: link care to checking an order. Applying is not a job offer: include selection stages. Support is not a guarantee: explain how it can help. A copied practice profile is not proof of an actual encounter. A file present is not automatically secure portfolio evidence.
ta_focus: Model: check vocabulary and source clue. Encounter: help access questions/replies, without supplying answers. Independent explanation: retain the learner’s thinking and actual prompts. Portfolio: help locate work, then ask the learner to judge it. Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task.
worked_example_and_fade: Profile A: the bakery values care. The shop assistant checks an order, which can prevent a wrong item. Applicants send an application, staff select people to meet, then use an interview and task before an offer decision. Written steps can help new staff learn a routine. Model A, then let learners use B or actual source evidence without copying.
check_after_model: Ask privately: which explains support, “they are nice” or “written steps help staff learn a routine”? The second names a support and its effect. Keep the source clue.

delivery_modes.Visitor mode: Brief the employer/employee on roles, valued skills, recruitment, progression and culture/support. Agree question methods, access and outcomes. Let each learner ask or relay a question and receive a response, with follow-up. Record the actual source, date, purpose and participation in the controlled school record. No named employer is placed in this pack.
delivery_modes.Recorded talk mode: Use an approved local recording with captions/transcript. Pause for facts and questions. Record what was heard and what is still missing. If an actual employer response is later arranged, log it then. Playback or a teacher discussion alone does not show two-way employer interaction.
delivery_modes.No visitor or recording mode: Read A or B. An adult answers from the printed response bank in a clearly labelled simulation. Learners ask, listen and follow up, then explain the same three outcome parts. Unknown facts stay unknown. Assess explanation skills from the profile; keep real employer encounter status not yet.

employer_profiles.roles: A baker makes bread. A shop assistant serves people and checks orders. A team leader plans the work.
employer_profiles.skills: Staff value care, clear talk and team work. A shop assistant checks an order and asks if a detail is unclear. This helps the team give the right items.
employer_profiles.recruitment: First, read the role details and send an application with a skill example. Staff select people to meet. Next comes an interview and a short order-check task. Staff compare the evidence before deciding whom to offer a role. Applying alone does not mean a job offer.
employer_profiles.support: New staff get written task steps and a buddy to ask for help. This can help a person learn a new routine and check a step they do not yet know.
employer_profiles.culture: Staff explain new words and invite questions. A private check-in gives space to ask for help. Belonging includes being heard and treated with respect.
employer_profiles.progression: With training and evidence of skills, a worker could apply for more tasks or a team leader role. A later role has its own checks and is not promised.
employer_profiles.unknown: Pay, hours, entry grades, age rules, travel, dates and real jobs are not given. Ask about these before a real choice.

employer_profiles.roles: A stock worker checks goods and records where they go. A dispatch worker checks orders. A team leader plans the shift.
employer_profiles.skills: Staff value accuracy, safe choices and clear messages. A stock worker checks an item code against the order and asks about a mismatch. Guessing could send the wrong item.
employer_profiles.recruitment: First, read the role details and send an application with a skill example. Staff select people to meet. Next comes an interview and a short paper stock-check task. Staff compare the evidence before deciding whom to offer a role. Applying alone does not mean a job offer.
employer_profiles.support: New staff see a task model, practise with a buddy and use a clear checklist. This can help a person learn the steps and spot a missed check.
employer_profiles.culture: Staff can raise a concern and ask for a step to be shown again. A private check-in helps them discuss support. The example values questions as part of safe work.
employer_profiles.progression: With training and evidence of skills, a worker could apply for stock control or a team leader role. Further training and selection may be needed.
employer_profiles.unknown: Pay, hours, entry grades, age rules, travel, dates and real jobs are not given. Support in a real job needs to be discussed.

portfolio_rule: The Evidence Sheet indexes all seven scheme outputs with work references, held/missing/partial status, quality check and next action. Keep Weeks 2–3 prepared-source labels and Week 6 real/simulated mode. Check actual work rather than ticking attendance. A portfolio can be reviewed and closed with clearly recorded gaps; do not mark all outcomes secure because the folder exists.
earlier_profile_rule: Compare one earlier strength, interest or work preference with a detail from the encounter. State a match, a changed view or a question with a reason. If the Autumn 1 profile is unavailable, record missing and date a brief current baseline; do not invent a past view or claim the comparison is complete.
encounter_evidence_rule: I15 requires preparation, clear outcomes, two-way employer/employee interaction and reflection. Record actual employer/source reference, date, purpose and participation in the school record. Simulation can show explanation skills; it cannot establish an actual employer encounter. Recorded-only replies may remain pending. Keep real contact status separate from learning evidence.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Employer encounter — skills, recruitment and belonging
GROW · up to five learners · 40-minute classroom example · assessing week
Unit: Identity & Belonging — Belonging in work
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
I can explain what the employer looks for, how recruitment works and one way the workplace supports people to succeed.
Weekly outcome: Students learn directly from an employer about work, valued skills, recruitment and workplace inclusion.

Source: specialist Careers scheme, GROW Careers physical row 15 / Autumn 2 row 7. E15 intention; F15 focus; G15 outcome; H15 sequence; I15 encounter structure; J15 evidence; K15 access; L15 support; M15 end check; N15 S.
What can an employer tell me about getting work and being supported at work?
1. Explain one valued skill with evidence. 2. Explain recruitment steps and what is used to select people. 3. Explain one workplace support and how it helps someone succeed.

Books, pens, profile A/B, question menu, vocabulary, evidence record and the seven weeks of work already held. Have the Autumn 1 personal career profile ready if available. Staff may use a visitor or approved local recording with captions/transcript. No visitor or recording is supplied. Without either, use the complete printed role-play.

I15 calls for preparation, clear outcomes, two-way employer/employee interaction and structured reflection. It specifies no phase minutes. The 5/5/12/10/8 classroom example is an adaptation. Allow a longer or separate real encounter if needed; prepare before and reflect after it. Profile simulation and recording alone are learning sources, not proof of a real employer encounter. The user adds a seven-week portfolio close to J15.
This helps me prepare for an application, ask about support and choose a useful next step towards work.
Retrieve a valued skill or working preference. Revisit the earlier personal profile privately. Choose a question about roles, skills, recruitment, progression or culture.
Model skill plus source clue, recruitment sequence and support plus effect. Rehearse a learner question privately; agree normal access.
Use visitor, approved recording or profile role-play. Record source, question/reply status and evidence. Preserve time for questions and follow-up.
Learners explain all three outcome parts. Link the new evidence to the earlier personal profile. Retain first response, support and one revision.
Locate Weeks 1–7 outputs. Record actual references, evidence status, gaps and one action. Close with a personal next step.

5 + 5 + 12 + 10 + 8 = 40 minutes. Collect earlier work before the lesson so the final check is realistic. Missing work becomes a dated catch-up action; do not recreate a half-term in eight minutes. A real event may need a separate or longer window.

Brief the employer/employee on roles, valued skills, recruitment, progression and culture/support. Agree question methods, access and outcomes. Let each learner ask or relay a question and receive a response, with follow-up. Record the actual source, date, purpose and participation in the controlled school record. No named employer is placed in this pack.

Use an approved local recording with captions/transcript. Pause for facts and questions. Record what was heard and what is still missing. If an actual employer response is later arranged, log it then. Playback or a teacher discussion alone does not show two-way employer interaction.

Read A or B. An adult answers from the printed response bank in a clearly labelled simulation. Learners ask, listen and follow up, then explain the same three outcome parts. Unknown facts stay unknown. Assess explanation skills from the profile; keep real employer encounter status not yet.

Select source evidence for a valued skill, explain the recruitment sequence and selection evidence, and show how one support helps. Compare with the earlier personal profile and keep a next question. Locate all seven portfolio outputs and identify any gap.

Read one profile section or talk section at a time. Use the question menu, separate model, word bank and three explanation headings. Rehearse privately. Fade answer frames where secure. Keep the learner’s own explanation and portfolio judgements.

Use A and short choices. Read or scribe the learner’s own response. Then ask them to explain the chosen skill with a clue, place recruitment steps in order, and say how a support helps. Choices alone are partial. Adult help finding work can support portfolio access without deciding the evidence judgement.

Use explicit instruction, a worked model, guided practice and a visible sequence. Chunk the profile into role, skill, recruitment and support. Keep a checklist and use retrieval from actual earlier work. Allow processing time.

Pre-teach employer, recruitment, evidence and belonging. Use private rehearsal, written questions, a scribe or relay of the learner’s own words. Check access to replies. No cold calling. Accept speech, writing, pointing with explanation, or normal communication aids.

Explain who will speak and how the session will run. No forced public disclosure of grades, diagnosis, family employment or income. Allow a private view, a regulation break and a clear return point. Missing portfolio work is an action to plan, not a public judgement.

Use clear print, captions/transcript, accessible seating and normal aids. Check hearing, sightlines and comfort. The lesson uses source reading only; no bakery equipment, lifting, machinery or practical workplace task is required.

Plan in any language. Use the vocabulary and short frames, pause the source and check key meanings. Separate language access from careers understanding. Normal reading/scribing aids continue while answer scaffolds fade.

Profile A: the bakery values care. The shop assistant checks an order, which can prevent a wrong item. Applicants send an application, staff select people to meet, then use an interview and task before an offer decision. Written steps can help new staff learn a routine. Model A, then let learners use B or actual source evidence without copying.
Ask privately: which explains support, “they are nice” or “written steps help staff learn a routine”? The second names a support and its effect. Keep the source clue.

A learner says “I applied, so I have the job.” A agree, or B staff still select and check evidence before an offer decision? B. If any learner is unsure, sequence the profile steps with them before independent explanation. If secure, ask why the task provides relevant evidence.

“A checklist means nobody can make a mistake.” A agree, or B it can help someone spot a missed check but does not guarantee success? B. If insecure, model support plus likely effect and a limit, then revisit a different example.

A skill label alone is not an evidence-based explanation: link care to checking an order. Applying is not a job offer: include selection stages. Support is not a guarantee: explain how it can help. A copied practice profile is not proof of an actual encounter. A file present is not automatically secure portfolio evidence.

Floor: “They value ... . The card says ... .” Medium: “First ... then ... . Staff use ... to choose.” High: “This support may help because ... . My earlier profile said ... . I now think ... because ... .”

Model: check vocabulary and source clue. Encounter: help access questions/replies, without supplying answers. Independent explanation: retain the learner’s thinking and actual prompts. Portfolio: help locate work, then ask the learner to judge it. Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task.

N15 S: assess the three exact outcome parts using actual source evidence. Record secure, partial or not yet for valued skill, recruitment and workplace support separately. M15 checks a recruitment insight and valued skill with encounter evidence; the exact outcome also requires workplace support. The new reflection links to the earlier personal career profile.

Compare one earlier strength, interest or work preference with a detail from the encounter. State a match, a changed view or a question with a reason. If the Autumn 1 profile is unavailable, record missing and date a brief current baseline; do not invent a past view or claim the comparison is complete.

The Evidence Sheet indexes all seven scheme outputs with work references, held/missing/partial status, quality check and next action. Keep Weeks 2–3 prepared-source labels and Week 6 real/simulated mode. Check actual work rather than ticking attendance. A portfolio can be reviewed and closed with clearly recorded gaps; do not mark all outcomes secure because the folder exists.

I15 requires preparation, clear outcomes, two-way employer/employee interaction and reflection. Record actual employer/source reference, date, purpose and participation in the school record. Simulation can show explanation skills; it cannot establish an actual employer encounter. Recorded-only replies may remain pending. Keep real contact status separate from learning evidence.

Generic employer types only. Profiles are invented, not offers, universal recruitment rules or support guarantees. No actual learner history or attendance is prefilled. No public personal disclosure or real practical work. Use controlled references instead of adding named employers to the distributed pack.

Book first. Optional Type instead carries the same demand. Record usual access separately from answer prompts. Set one NS, allow a learner revision and preserve first thinking. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

VF verbal feedback · WS worked with support · I independent · NS next step in green · // self-edit · ? read this back · E actual banked evidence · R only after Voice, Audience, NS and a response in the learner’s in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.
This closes Autumn 2 Careers. Spring 1 work awaits the owner’s acceptance and new brief.

GROW Careers · Year A · up to five learners
Autumn 2 Week 7 · 14–18 December 2026 · Tuesday 15 December · P3

GROW Careers physical row 15 / Autumn 2 row 7; E15–N15

Can the student identify one recruitment insight and one employer-valued skill with evidence from the encounter?
S source marker; assessing week. Independent / Supported / Floor. Normal aids, private responses and no cold calling.

Visitor: actual employer questions/replies and reflection. Recording: facts with any employer replies pending. Fallback: full A/B profiles and adult response bank, clearly simulated. Assess explanation skills separately from real encounter completion.

I15 gives preparation, clear outcomes, two-way interaction and structured reflection, with source/date/purpose/participation recorded. It has no fixed phase minutes. The 5/5/12/10/8 plan is illustrative. Allow a separate or longer real event if needed.

Gather earlier work before the lesson. Index all seven outputs, check quality and source/mode labels, record actual references and missing/partial work, and agree one dated action. Compare with Autumn 1 personal profile. Missing history remains missing; a newly dated baseline does not replace it.
This helps me prepare for an application, ask about support and choose a useful next step towards work.

Question menu, separate model, profiles, vocabulary, private rehearsal, captions/transcript and normal aids. Plan in any language. No grades, diagnosis, family work or income disclosure. Keep usual access and answer prompts separate. Offer to the Communication portfolio. E for banked evidence; R after Voice, Audience, NS and response in in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.

Week 7 summative. No clock time or actual visitor attendance asserted. Spring 1 waits for a new brief after acceptance.

Source E15–N15. Week 7 assessment marker S. H15 covers roles, skills, recruitment, progression, culture and reflective comparison with the Autumn 1 personal profile. I15 requires preparation, outcomes, two-way interaction and reflection; there are no fixed phase minutes.
Actual source clues, questions/replies and three-part explanation.
Log actual employer/source reference, date, purpose, participation and reflection.
Attributable information and questions; later replies if they happen.
Playback alone does not establish two-way employer contact.
A/B role-play plus sourced explanation and profile link.
Simulated learning evidence; real encounter not yet.

Prepare the learner enquiry, question method and access. Brief a visitor on the five topic areas. Preview local media and transcript. Have earlier portfolio work ready and sort by week before the final eight-minute check. If none of this is available, the full profile fallback needs only this pack and books.

Normal aids stay available in the assessing week. Log adult answer help and distinguish it from reading/scribing. Record the first explanation before feedback, then a revision. Apply secure/partial/not yet separately to the three outcome parts. Portfolio presence, attendance and real encounter status are separate judgements.
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented examples. They describe no real employer, vacancy or offer.
Care, clear talk and team work.
Accuracy, safe choices and clear messages.
Check an order; ask about unclear detail.
Check an item code; ask about mismatch.
Application, selection, interview and order-check task, offer decision.
Application, selection, interview and paper stock-check task, offer decision.
Learn routine and check unknown step.
Learn steps and spot missed check.
Raise concerns, repeat a step, private check-in.

A: “They value care because the assistant checks an order. Staff read applications, choose people to meet and use an interview and task before deciding on an offer. Written steps can help new staff learn a routine.” B: “Accuracy matters because the worker checks the code. Staff use an application, interview and stock task to select people. A checklist can help staff spot a missed check.”

These are examples, not scripts learners must copy. Do not award secure merely for repeating the model with no source understanding. Accept an equivalent explanation in the learner’s own words or normal communication mode.
“Written steps help staff learn a routine” names both support and likely effect. “They are nice” gives no clear support mechanism. Look for the source clue.
B: application alone does not mean a job offer. Order the selection steps from the card. The short task gives relevant evidence; it does not guarantee selection.
B: a checklist can help someone notice a missed check, but does not guarantee success. Use can or may when explaining likely effects.
A, A, B, A, B, A. Follow with the skill clue, recruitment explanation and support-effect link. Choices alone are partial. Record answer prompts separately from normal access.

A skill label needs a clue. Selection happens after an application. Support can improve access without guaranteeing a result. A positive judgement is not required. Profile role-play is not real employer contact. Missing work is not completed work. A current baseline is not proof of a historical view.

Accept a match, changed view or uncertainty linked to an actual earlier strength, interest or preference and new evidence. Keep the older work reference. If unavailable, record missing and a dated current baseline; comparison remains due. Do not infer personal needs from diagnosis or task behaviour.

No forced public response or disclosure of grades, health, family employment or income. A learner may give their reflection privately. Use controlled source references; the distributed pack contains no named employers or learner records.
Explain sector and job. Map roles in at least four sectors.
Keep source and date. Use a data clue and give a cautious view. Mark practice data.
Use more than one card for each job. Keep what is alike, what differs and open questions.
Compare at least three ways. Explain what fits your preferences.
Map two routes. Show what skills, experience or study each needs.
Keep question status, entry facts and own-needs view. Mark real or practice.
Explain a valued skill, recruitment and support. Link to your earlier profile.

Locate each actual output and record a book/file reference. Mark held, partial or missing. Check content, source labels and support; presence alone does not show a secure outcome. Week 2 uses illustrative data with source/date, Week 3 uses prepared sources, and Week 6 retains real/simulated status and own-needs evidence. Week 7 keeps the three-part explanation and earlier profile link.

Agree one manageable next action with support and review date. Keep any other gaps visible. Missing work can be caught up later and dated then; never backdate or fabricate an output. Review and portfolio closure do not mean every outcome or real encounter is complete.

M15 requires a recruitment insight and valued skill with evidence; also check support for G15. Keep the first explanation and revision. Offer to the Communication portfolio. E for actual banked evidence; R after Voice, Audience, NS and response in in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Staff confirm any accredited mapping. This closes Autumn 2; wait for the new Spring 1 brief.
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented examples. They describe no real employer, vacancy or offer.
A baker makes bread. A shop assistant serves people and checks orders. A team leader plans the work.
Staff value care, clear talk and team work. A shop assistant checks an order and asks if a detail is unclear. This helps the team give the right items.

First, read the role details and send an application with a skill example. Staff select people to meet. Next comes an interview and a short order-check task. Staff compare the evidence before deciding whom to offer a role. Applying alone does not mean a job offer.
New staff get written task steps and a buddy to ask for help. This can help a person learn a new routine and check a step they do not yet know.
Staff explain new words and invite questions. A private check-in gives space to ask for help. Belonging includes being heard and treated with respect.
With training and evidence of skills, a worker could apply for more tasks or a team leader role. A later role has its own checks and is not promised.
Pay, hours, entry grades, age rules, travel, dates and real jobs are not given. Ask about these before a real choice.
Read and discuss only. No real work task, equipment or site visit is part of this card.
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented examples. They describe no real employer, vacancy or offer.
A stock worker checks goods and records where they go. A dispatch worker checks orders. A team leader plans the shift.
Staff value accuracy, safe choices and clear messages. A stock worker checks an item code against the order and asks about a mismatch. Guessing could send the wrong item.

First, read the role details and send an application with a skill example. Staff select people to meet. Next comes an interview and a short paper stock-check task. Staff compare the evidence before deciding whom to offer a role. Applying alone does not mean a job offer.
New staff see a task model, practise with a buddy and use a clear checklist. This can help a person learn the steps and spot a missed check.
Staff can raise a concern and ask for a step to be shown again. A private check-in helps them discuss support. The example values questions as part of safe work.
With training and evidence of skills, a worker could apply for stock control or a team leader role. Further training and selection may be needed.
Pay, hours, entry grades, age rules, travel, dates and real jobs are not given. Support in a real job needs to be discussed.
Read and discuss only. No real work task, equipment or site visit is part of this card.
Choose a question with a clear purpose. You may write it or ask an adult to relay your own words.
What do people do in this workplace?
Which skill matters, and how do staff show it?
What happens after I apply? What evidence do you use?
How could a worker learn more or move to another role?
How do new staff get help and feel part of the team?
“I want to find out ... . My question is ... . This matters because ... .” Rehearse in private if it helps.
Keep a skill clue, recruitment steps and one support. Ask a follow-up if a reply is unclear. Mark a missing fact as a gap.
Explain what the employer values, how staff are chosen and how one support can help. Compare a clue with your earlier personal profile. Keep one next question.
Visitor reply, recorded fact and adult practice reply are different sources. Mark what actually happened. Plan in any language.

The bakery values care. A shop assistant checks an order, which can help avoid wrong items. Staff read applications, select people to meet, then use an interview and task before an offer decision. Written steps can help a new worker learn a routine.
Practice profile link: “My earlier profile said I like clear steps. The written steps could help me. I would ask how I can get help if a step is unclear.” This is a model, not your past view.
Use profile A. An adult may read or scribe your own choices.
A: Checks an order with care. B: Is just good at everything.
A: Apply, then selection and checks. B: Apply and the job is yours.
A: No help is needed. B: Written steps can help with a new routine.
A: Staff can ask and be heard. B: Nobody can ask a question.
A: The role-play proves a real visit. B: Mark the profile exchange as practice.
A: Keep a gap and plan an action. B: Tick work that is missing.
Choices alone are not the full task. Explain the skill clue, recruitment steps and how support helps. Link to your own earlier profile if it is available. Keep missing work honest.
Tell learners this is role-play. Answer from A or B, allow a follow-up and keep missing facts as gaps.
Stock worker, dispatch worker, team leader.
Care, clear talk, team work. Check an order and ask about unclear details.
Accuracy, safe choices, clear messages. Check a code and ask about a mismatch.
Application with skill example; selection; interview and order-check task; offer decision.
Application with skill example; selection; interview and paper stock-check task; offer decision.
Written steps and buddy can help with a new routine and an unknown step.
Task model, buddy and checklist can help learn steps and spot missed checks.
Questions, clear words, private check-in and respect.
Raise a concern, ask for a repeat, private support check-in.
Training and evidence may support an application for more tasks or team leader.
Training and evidence may support stock control or team leader applications.
For pay, hours, grades, age, travel, dates or actual vacancies: “This practice card does not tell us. Keep that question for a real employer.”
